I often re-read books. They don't really stick with me, so I can generally enjoy them just as much a second time, and if they're particularly good, I can enjoy them every few years, even if I've read them enough times that I remember all the details.

Some books I've re-read so many times that I've lost track of how many times I've re-read them:

TItus Groan and Gormenghast by Mervyn Peake (the source of my username)

Catch-22 by Joseph Heller

The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (series) by Douglas Adams

The Book of the New Sun (series) by Gene Wolfe

When Gravity Fails by George Alec Effinger

A Confederacy of Dunces by John Kennedy Toole

Roadmarks by Roger Zelazny

All of the Sherlock Holmes stories, by Arthur Conan Doyle. I got a complete set of the books in paperback when I was a kid, then a hardcover omnibus edition of the complete works years later, and I read one or the other, from start to finish, every few years.

Hardwired and Voice of the Whirlwind by Walter Jon Williams

Lots of Vonnegut - the most notable ones would be Slapstick, Breakfast of Champions, Sirens of Titan, Cats Cradle and God Bless You Mr. Rosewater.

Some Tom Robbins - particularly Jitterbug Perfume.

Demian by Hermann Hesse

Stand on Zanzibar and The Sheep Look Up by John Brunner

I'm sure there are more, but that's all I can think of right off...

That's something I can't do. I've tried with books I've liked (especially when there's years worth of wait between releases), but if I remember what's going on it just doesn't hold my interest.

The entire Star Trek: New Frontier series by Peter David.
